title: Eggplant Emoji 🍆 Meaning: The Internet’s Rudest Vegetable
description: The 🍆 eggplant emoji is the standard symbol for a penis in texting and social media. Learn where the slang came from and when it still means dinner.
summary: The 🍆 eggplant emoji is used almost universally to mean a penis. It appears in sexting, dirty jokes and thirst comments, and only rarely refers to the vegetable. Because the sexual meaning is so well known, sending it to the wrong person can cause real embarrassment.
meaning: Ask nearly any adult with a phone what 🍆 means and you will not hear about parmigiana. The long, purple, slightly curved vegetable became the go-to symbol for a penis early in the smartphone era, and it has held the title ever since. It can signal arousal, an invitation to sex, a brag, or a joke about any of those. The meaning is fixed enough that brands, comedians and sex-education campaigns all rely on it.

Platforms have noticed. In 2015 Instagram blocked searches for the eggplant hashtag while leaving other suggestive emojis searchable, a decision that drew plenty of mockery. Later moderation rules on Facebook and Instagram named the eggplant and peach as examples of emojis that count as sexual when paired with a solicitation. Those episodes confirmed what users already knew: this is a rude emoji that happens to look like produce.

Humor softens it. Much of the time 🍆 is not a serious proposition but a punchline, used to tease a friend about a date, to react to a shirtless photo, or to mock someone's swagger (“big 🍆 energy”). The literal vegetable does still exist in cooking posts, gardening updates and menus, where surrounding food words make the meaning safe. Outside North America the same emoji is called an aubergine or a brinjal, and the slang travels with it.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: In a private chat with someone you are attracted to, 🍆 is sexual, full stop. It can open a sexting exchange or answer a suggestive photo. Among friends it is more often comic, as in reacting to gossip about a hookup. Sent unprompted to someone who has not signaled interest, it is the emoji version of a crude remark.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Comment sections use it to express thirst over a celebrity or creator, frequently alongside 💦 or 🥵. It also helps people avoid typing explicit words that moderation systems flag. Because platforms treat it as sexual in context, posts combining it with offers or requests can be removed.

contexts.label: In cooking and gardening
contexts.body: Recipe writers and vegetable gardeners use it straight, for baba ganoush, ratatouille or a summer harvest. They generally know the joke is coming and either lean into it or add other vegetables like 🍅 and 🧄 so the dish is clearly the subject. In a grocery list between partners, nobody is confused.

examples.meaning: A friend nosily asking whether things got physical.
A literal dinner plan, made clear by the other ingredients.

examples.text: He walks in like he's got big 🍆 energy
examples.meaning: Teasing someone for acting overly confident or macho.
A gardener proudly showing homegrown eggplants.
A thirst comment expressing sexual attraction to someone.

combos.meaning: Sex, particularly penetrative sex; the most common explicit emoji pairing.
Cooking with eggplant; the extra ingredients keep it literal.

confusedWith.difference: 🍌 can also mean a penis, but it is sillier and far more often literal. The eggplant is the default and reads as sexual with no help from context; the banana needs a wink to get there.
🍑 represents a butt, not a penis. The two complete each other in sexual messages, which is why they are so often confused as “the same kind of emoji” while meaning different things.
🌭 is occasionally used as phallic humor, yet it mostly means cookouts and ballgames. It lacks the eggplant's automatic innuendo.

avoid: Never send it to coworkers, clients, relatives or anyone who has not invited that kind of message.
Don't send it unsolicited to someone you are pursuing; it is widely experienced as harassment rather than flirting.
Keep it out of public brand or business posts unless the joke is fully intended.
design: The emoji depicts a single deep-purple eggplant with a green stem cap, generally drawn at a diagonal. Proportions differ a little, with some versions longer and slimmer and others plumper, and highlights vary in glossiness. No vendor's design changes the meaning; the shape that inspired the slang is present on every platform.

faqs.q: Why does the eggplant emoji mean a penis?
faqs.a: Its shape. Among the early food emojis, the eggplant was the most phallic, and users adopted it for that purpose within a few years of emoji keyboards becoming common. Repetition in memes and media made the meaning standard.

faqs.q: What does 🍆 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: The same thing it means from anyone: a reference to a penis or to sex. She might be flirting, joking with friends or reacting to someone attractive. Tone and relationship tell you whether it is an invitation or just humor.

faqs.q: Can I use 🍆 for actual eggplant?
faqs.a: You can, and cooks do, but expect a joke in reply. Surround it with other ingredients or type the word to keep things clear. In professional food writing many people skip the emoji altogether.

faqs.q: Is the eggplant emoji banned on Instagram?
faqs.a: The emoji itself is allowed. Instagram once blocked hashtag searches for it, and Meta's rules treat it as sexual when it accompanies a request or offer for sexual contact. Ordinary joking use is not removed.
It is a play on “big dick energy,” a slang phrase for quiet, unforced confidence. Written with the emoji it is typically used with a wink, either as a compliment or to poke fun at someone's bravado.
